concepts.short: The middle forecast if returns stay close to the fund’s long-term track record.
concepts.detail: We blend each fund’s 10-year, 5-year, or 3-year rolling CAGR (whichever is available) using your split. This is not a promise — it is the arithmetic midpoint for planning.

concepts.short: A pessimistic path: base return minus 4 percentage points.
concepts.detail: Markets can deliver below-average decades (Japan 1990s, India 2008–2013 for many funds). Bear case asks: if returns are weaker than history, what do you still end up with? Use this for stress-testing, not fear.

concepts.short: An optimistic path: base return plus 2 percentage points.
concepts.detail: A strong equity cycle (like 2016–2021 for mid/small caps) can beat long-term averages for a while. Bull case caps at 22% so numbers stay realistic. Do not plan your life around bull alone.

concepts.short: The smoothed yearly return that turns your starting money into the ending value.
concepts.detail: If ₹30 lakh becomes ₹1.5 crore in 15 years, CAGR is about 11.5% per year — even if some years were +40% and others −20%. SIP makes this harder to feel intuitively; that is why we show year-by-year tables.

concepts.short: How much of fund A’s portfolio is also inside fund B.
concepts.detail: Computed as the sum of min(weight in A, weight in B) across common stocks. Two ‘different’ funds with 35% overlap are partly the same bet. Under 20% = low, 20–40% = moderate, 40%+ = high.

concepts.short: The worst peak-to-trough fall before recovering.
concepts.detail: If your ₹10L became ₹6L at the bottom of COVID (2020), that is a 40% drawdown. For 15-year SIPs, drawdowns on paper are normal. Selling during drawdown is what turns paper loss into real loss.

concepts.short: Manager can invest anywhere across large, mid, and small without fixed limits.
concepts.detail: One fund can act as your core. Many flexi funds are actually large-cap heavy in practice — read the factsheet, not just the label.

concepts.short: Direct = lower expense ratio; same stocks and same tax on withdrawal.
concepts.detail: Direct saves roughly 0.5–1% per year in TER. Over 15 years that compounding matters. Tax (STCG 20%, LTCG 12.5% after ₹1.25L) is identical for Direct and Regular Growth.

concepts.short: Fixed amount invested every month automatically.
concepts.detail: ₹15,000/month for 15 years = 180 instalments = ₹27 lakh of SIP + ₹3 lakh lumpsum = ₹30 lakh total invested. Early instalments have more time to compound; recent instalments are still short-term for tax if sold.

large_cap.label: Large cap
large_cap.sebi: Top 100 stocks by market cap (Nifty 100-ish universe).
large_cap.risk: Lowest volatility in equity; drawdowns ~35–40% in crashes.
large_cap.role: Anchor / core — use when you want smoother 15-year ride.

mid_cap.label: Mid cap
mid_cap.risk: Higher vol than large; can lag for years then catch up.
mid_cap.role: Growth engine — 20–40% of a long portfolio, not 100%.

small_cap.label: Small cap
small_cap.risk: Highest vol; 45–50% drawdowns are normal. Liquidity risk in stress.
small_cap.role: Satellite only — 10–25% for 15+ year horizon if you can hold through pain.

flexi_cap.label: Flexi cap
flexi_cap.sebi: Fund manager chooses across large, mid, and small with no fixed band.
flexi_cap.risk: Depends on how the manager runs it — many flexi funds are large-heavy.
flexi_cap.role: One-stop core — good as primary fund if overlap with second fund is low.

multi_cap.label: Multi cap
multi_cap.sebi: Must invest at least 25% each in large, mid, and small (SEBI rule).
multi_cap.risk: Balanced by mandate; still equity risk.
multi_cap.role: Structured all-cap exposure — alternative to flexi + mid/small pair.

large_mid_cap.label: Large & mid cap
large_mid_cap.sebi: Large + mid only; no small-cap mandate.
large_mid_cap.risk: Between large and mid; less wild than pure mid/small.
large_mid_cap.role: Middle ground core when you do not want small-cap satellite.

combo_presets.label: Flexi + Mid
combo_presets.hint: Classic expert split: one flexi core (manager picks across caps) plus a mid-cap growth engine. Example: PPFAS Flexi + HDFC Mid Cap.

combo_presets.label: Flexi + Small
combo_presets.hint: Most popular 15-year pair: flexi does the heavy lifting; small cap adds alpha with 20–30% satellite weight.

combo_presets.label: Flexi + Large & Mid
combo_presets.hint: No small-cap mandate. Flexi core + large&mid for digital/industrial tilt without full small-cap volatility.

combo_presets.label: Large + Mid
combo_presets.hint: Large-cap anchor for smoother ride; mid cap for growth. Good if you want less flexi-manager risk.

combo_presets.label: Large + Small
combo_presets.hint: Barbell: large-cap safety net with a small-cap kicker. Keep small at 20–25% mentally even if you type 25%.

combo_presets.label: Multi + Small
combo_presets.hint: Multi-cap is mandated 25/25/25 across caps; small satellite on top. Structured core + aggressive tail.

combo_presets.label: Flexi + Multi
combo_presets.hint: Two all-cap styles: manager-driven flexi vs SEBI-mandated multi. Check overlap — can be moderate.

combo_presets.label: Large & Mid + Mid
combo_presets.hint: Both mid-heavy categories — experts rarely do this. Use only if you understand overlap will be high.

combo_presets.label: Large + Large & Mid
combo_presets.hint: Conservative blend: pure large plus large&mid. Lower vol than flexi+small; lower upside too.

combo_presets.label: Mid + Small
combo_presets.hint: Aggressive all-growth pair. Only for 15+ year horizon and stomach for 45%+ drawdowns. Not a beginner combo.

expert_pairs.title: Core + satellite (most common expert split)
expert_pairs.why: One flexi core (PPFAS: India + global, low turnover) plus one small-cap satellite for long-term alpha. Different cap buckets; overlap usually low.
expert_pairs.bn: Nippon India Small Cap Fund Growth Plan

expert_pairs.title: Stable + growth (lower sleep loss)
expert_pairs.why: Large-cap anchor (ICICI Bluechip) + mid-cap engine (HDFC Mid). Classic 60/40 for 15 years: smoother than two aggressive funds.
expert_pairs.an: ICICI Prudential Large Cap Fund (erstwhile Bluechip Fund)

expert_pairs.title: Flexi core + mid engine
expert_pairs.why: PPFAS Flexi (quality + global) with HDFC Mid Cap. Classic 65/35: core does heavy lifting, mid adds growth without full small-cap volatility.

expert_pairs.title: HDFC flexi + small satellite
expert_pairs.why: HDFC Flexi (large-heavy India book) + Nippon Small Cap. Same AMC but different cap buckets; overlap stays moderate (~8%).
expert_pairs.bn: Nippon India Small Cap Fund Growth Plan

expert_pairs.title: Large-cap safety + mid-cap punch
expert_pairs.why: ICICI Bluechip (large anchor) + Motilal Oswal Midcap (digital/AI tilt). For investors who want large-cap sleep with mid-cap upside.
expert_pairs.an: ICICI Prudential Large Cap Fund (erstwhile Bluechip Fund)

expert_pairs.title: Transformation + ballast
expert_pairs.why: Kotak Multicap (flexible across caps) + SBI Large Cap (quality large names, some energy). Fits AI/EV/online theme without betting everything on small caps.

expert_pairs.title: Multi-cap structure + small alpha
expert_pairs.why: Kotak Multicap (mandated 25/25/25 across caps) + Invesco Smallcap. Structured core with a small-cap kicker.

expert_pairs.title: Value flexi + large & mid
expert_pairs.why: Canara Robeco Flexi + Mirae Large & Mid. Two different managers; overlap usually low; no small-cap mandate.

expert_pairs.title: Multi-cap + flexi (low overlap)
expert_pairs.why: ICICI Flexicap (EV-heavy book) + Mirae Large & Mid (digital/industrial). Different categories and managers; overlap typically under 25%.

expert_pairs.title: Two cores, different styles
expert_pairs.why: PPFAS (quality + foreign) and HDFC Flexi (India banks/industrials). Experts use this when you want two flexi names that behave differently — but check overlap (~32% historically).
